name: Remove layout destroying HTML-Tags
author: Stefano Picco

sections.description:
Copy&Paste Cleaner. If you want to quickly fill a post or a page with content that already exists, copy&paste is often used and it can destroy the layout of a website!

The basic problem is that if you copy&paste content from different sources into the visual editor, any formatting is copied over. Specifically, whether from text documents, other websites, online-shops and cms or even from social media, something comes along everywhere. This also applies to content generated in AI chats, which often contains unwanted formatting as well.

As there are often DIVs in addition to harmless HTML elements, these can cause the rendering of your own website to be faulty or interrupted. The integrated DIV-Detector automatically detects div elements in your content after pasting and shows a visual warning with a direct cleanup link.

To avoid this, this plugin checks the existing formatting and attributes and removes all those that could lead to a problem – with one click.

The cleanup includes:

  • Removes layout-breaking elements such as div and span as well as wrapper elements (figure, article, picture, aside, pre, blockquote) – the text is kept
  • Removes unnecessary attributes (e.g. classes, styles, IDs as well as aria-* and data-*) – alt texts of images on your own website are preserved
  • Removes style, script and iframe blocks including their content
  • Removes leftover CSS that comes along when you paste e-mails or Word documents
  • Removes emojis and hashtag links (e.g. from Instagram)
  • Removes images from foreign domains, local images are kept
  • Reduces repeated empty paragraphs and line breaks
  • Merges redundant nested formatting
  • Converts lists (e.g. from Word) into standards-compliant lists and cleans them up

If you copy and paste into the text editor, there is usually no problem.

Tested with these page builders:

  • Classic editor
  • Gutenberg
  • Divi 4.27
  • Elementor 4.3
  • WPBakery 9.0
  • Beaver Builder 2.11

Accessibility

The DIV warning in the Classic Editor is announced automatically by screen readers. Alt texts of images hosted on your own website are preserved during cleanup, so the accessibility of your content is not reduced. Cleaning up also converts presentational bold and italic markup into semantic strong and em elements.

Privacy GDPR

This plugin processes the analyzed and converted HTML only within the respective website. No content is stored or transferred to other servers or services for processing. No external analytics tools or tracking services are integrated or used. Data protection in accordance with the GDPR is therefore guaranteed at all times.
sections.installation:
Installation from within WordPress

  1. Visit Plugins > Add New.
  2. Search for Remove layout destroying HTML-Tags.
  3. Install and activate the Remove layout destroying HTML-Tags plugin.

Manual installation

  1. Upload the entire remove-layout-destroying-html-tags folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Visit Plugins.
  3. Activate the Remove layout destroying HTML-Tags plugin.
sections.faq:
Why are some img elements being removed?

External images — those whose src attribute points to a foreign domain — are removed for copyright, performance and security reasons. Images that are hosted on your own domain (relative paths or same-domain absolute URLs) are kept. You should always insert image data properly and equip it with the appropriate attributes, which is better for accessibility, SEO and GEO (Generative Engine Optimization).

Is it working with Beaver, Gutenberg, Divi, Elementor or WPBakery?

At the moment it works fine with Classic Editor, Gutenberg, Divi 4, Elementor, WPBakery and Beaver Builder. Integration for Divi 5 is in process.

Why are the aria-* and title attributes removed?

These attributes are important for accessibility, but should be added and adapted individually so that the context is maintained. The alt text of images hosted on your own website is kept.

Why are emojis being removed too?

Although emojis are based on the international Unicode, they are sometimes displayed differently. This means that an emoji can look completely different on iOS, Android and Windows and have a corresponding effect. These are filtered out to avoid misunderstandings in terms of content and to avoid potential display errors.

How does it work in Gutenberg?

There are two ways to use it in Gutenberg: you can clean up the entire post or page or just the content of a block. To clean up a block, simply use the icon in the toolbar. If you want to clean up the entire content at once, go to the sidebar and use the Clean up HTML button in the HTML Cleanup section.

How does it work in Beaver Builder?

In Beaver Builder the cleanup button appears directly above the text editor toolbar inside each text module. Simply click the button to clean up the HTML content of that module. A spinner indicates that the process is running, and the button briefly turns green once the cleanup is complete.

Do I still need the plugin in Gutenberg and Elementor 4?

Current versions of Gutenberg and the Atomic elements in Elementor 4 already filter out many unwanted elements, such as div and span, when you paste content and keep only a small set of formatting. The plugin is still useful for the Classic Editor, the classic Elementor Text Editor widget, Divi, WPBakery, Beaver Builder, Custom HTML blocks and existing content. It also removes emojis and hashtag links.
